title: Pareto-optimal control strategies in intrinsically nonequilibrium systems
authors: Gustavo A. L. Forão, Carlos E. Fiore, Jonas Berx
abstract: Thermodynamic control is typically formulated as the optimisation of a single objective, yet competing costs rarely admit a common optimum, so single-objective control captures only one corner of the achievable performance space. We develop a general framework for multi-objective thermodynamic control of intrinsically nonequilibrium systems that maps out the full Pareto front of optimal control strategies. We show that Pareto-optimal protocols generically consist of smooth branches connected by boundary jumps, and that the relative weights of the objectives combine with the physical parameters into a single intrinsic scale that alone governs the trade-off. Remarkably, this scale plays a double role: it parametrizes a single functional form that generates the entire front, and it defines control equivalence classes, in which systems with different parameters but the same scale share identical optimal strategies. We illustrate the framework for two paradigmatic systems that are experimentally accessible: transport of an active particle in a harmonic trap, and a cyclic quantum-dot engine. For both, we obtain the Pareto front and optimal strategies in closed form.
summary: The paper establishes a general theoretical framework for optimizing thermodynamic control in complex, nonequilibrium systems by treating competing costs simultaneously. It demonstrates that the optimal trade-off structure is governed by a single intrinsic scale parameter, which simplifies the analysis and reveals deep structural equivalences between different physical setups like active matter and quantum engines.
main_problem: The work is developing a general framework for multi-objective thermodynamic control, addressing that single-objective optimization fails to capture the full performance space defined by competing costs.
main_result: The optimal protocols are shown to generically consist of smooth branches connected by boundary jumps, and the entire trade-off structure collapses onto a single intrinsic scale parameterizing equivalence classes of optimal strategies.
method: The authors formulate the problem using multi-objective optimization via scalarization ($\Omega = \sum  eta_i C_i$), deriving optimality conditions from variational principles applied to generalized cost functionals.
model_or_system: Two paradigmatic systems are analyzed: an active particle in a harmonic trap governed by an overdamped Langevin equation, and a cyclic quantum-dot engine operating between two temperature baths. The general framework applies to intrinsically nonequilibrium systems.

main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the relative weights determine the trade-off structure, and in some cases, relies on specific boundary conditions or low-order polynomial representations for simplification.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Pareto front (showing the full set of optimal trade-offs) and corresponding optimal control protocols ($\lambda^*(t)$ or $\epsilon^*(t)$) for both the active particle and quantum dot engine.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the general multi-objective variational framework, applies it first to the active particle model (showing dependence on an effective activity scale), then extends it to the quantum dot engine (analyzing power vs. dissipation trade-offs), culminating in a unified understanding of how system parameters collapse into single governing scales.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, generalized mathematical tool for analyzing non-equilibrium thermodynamics that moves beyond simple efficiency maximization by mapping out the entire achievable performance landscape using multi-objective optimization techniques.
